name: The Prebendal Manor

layers.essential_history: [[c:In 1107 Henry I gave the old royal hall here to the Bishop of Lincoln. Excavations, shown on Time Team in 2004, found remains of an earlier timber hall, thought to be the hall King Cnut used.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:The Prebendal Manor and its tithe barn are sometimes open to visitors. Its gardens grow only plants known in England before 1485.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:In the manor yard, the chessboard is still set out. One square is marked with a scratch.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The chessboard]]
material: [[c:The pieces stand where the game ended.]]
[[c:The empty square is where the King's piece stood.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Which way did the thief go? (one word)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:EAST. The thief went east, towards the river.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:A scratch on the board says the thief went EAST.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:The countryside loop, about 3.9 km. Take the footpath south from beside the Prebendal Manor and follow it south across the fields for about 1.6 km to the lane at the bottom. Turn right along the lane for about 600 metres, then take the footpath on the right heading north-east back towards the village. Keep north to the field path just south of the village, turn right to Station Road and walk up past the Black Horse. Just beyond it, take the footpath on the left west across to St Mary's Close.]]
